toneOfVoice.summary: Plain English, empathetic, never jargon-first. Gentle and respectful about death — no cheerful gimmicks.
rules: Say 'your will' not 'testamentary instrument' unless the legal term is explained inline.
Every legal term gets a 'What does this mean?' tooltip.
Use 'when you die' gently; avoid humour, exclamation marks, and confetti.
Sentences under 20 words where possible. Active voice.
Reassure, don't alarm: flags are 'a lawyer will look at this', never 'problem detected'.

tooltipExamples.executor: The person you choose to carry out the instructions in your will — a bit like the project manager of your estate.
tooltipExamples.guardian: The person who would look after your children day-to-day if both parents died.
tooltipExamples.residue: Everything left over after debts, expenses and any specific gifts have been paid out.
tooltipExamples.probate: The Supreme Court's official approval that lets your executor access accounts and property.
tooltipExamples.intestacy: What happens if someone dies without a valid will — the law decides who inherits.
